process:2.en: Grey Crow had left a data chip taped behind a broken vent in the old port warehouse. Its single file was a map — not of streets, but of steps. Each node was labeled: intercept, decode, transmit. 'Follow the *process*,' a recorded voice said, 'or the message dies with you.'
process:2.cnHint: 旧港仓库的通风口后，藏着一张描绘任务____的芯片。
process:2.hook: The final step on the map was simply marked: 'You.'
process:2.line: 'Follow the *process* exactly, or everything falls apart.'

able:2.en: The signal jammer filled the narrow server room with white noise. I pressed my ear to the cold wall, straining to catch Zero's transmission. For ten long seconds nothing came through. Then the noise broke — I was *able* to hear three words, low and clear, before silence swallowed them again.
able:2.cnHint: 干扰器让房间里全是噪音，但我终于____听清了三个词。
able:2.hook: Those three words changed everything I thought I knew.
able:2.line: 'I was finally *able* to hear what Zero was hiding.'

drive:2.en: The encrypted note was small, printed on paper thin as skin, tucked inside a cracked street lantern on Dock Nine. It read: 'What you call duty, others call *drive* — the force that pushes a person past every warning sign.' Ali looked at me. Neither of us spoke.
drive:2.cnHint: 路灯里藏着一张纸条，上面写着____是推着人越过一切警告的力量。
drive:2.hook: Ali's silence told me she had read that line before.
drive:2.line: 'Is it duty — or *drive* — that brought you this far?'

face:2.en: The stolen broadcast showed no body, only a pale *face* filling the screen — still, unreadable, like a mask pressed against glass. Zero had sent it as a warning. Ali froze beside me. Grey Crow's voice crackled through my earpiece: 'That image is a key. Read the shadows, not the skin.'
face:2.cnHint: 被盗播的画面上只有一张____，零点用它作为警告。
face:2.hook: The shadows on that face spelled out coordinates.
face:2.line: 'Study the *face* — what you see is not what is there.'

possible:2.en: The cipher on the warehouse wall used forty symbols. I photographed it and ran every pattern I knew. Two readings were *possible*: a time, or a location. They could not both be right — and choosing wrong meant walking into whatever Zero had prepared on the other end.
possible:2.cnHint: 仓库墙上的密码有两种____的解读，选错一种将是陷阱。
possible:2.hook: I picked one, folded the photo, and started walking.
possible:2.line: 'Two readings are *possible*. Only one leads out alive.'

similar:2.en: Ali spread three intercepted notes across the floor of the relay station. The handwriting, the paper weight, the ink — all *similar*, almost too close to be chance. 'Zero doesn't repeat patterns,' she said quietly, turning the third note over. A second message was written on the back.
similar:2.cnHint: 三张截获的纸条外观____，背面却藏着另一条信息。
similar:2.hook: The hidden message was addressed to my name.
similar:2.line: 'The style is *similar* — someone wants us to think they match.'

involve:2.en: Grey Crow's file on Zero was thinner than I expected. One line stood out: 'All known operations *involve* a decoy signal sent exactly nine minutes before the real one.' I checked the timestamp on the broadcast Ali and I had chased all night. It was a decoy. We had nine minutes left.
involve:2.cnHint: 档案显示零点的每次行动都____一个诱饵信号，而我们追错了目标。
involve:2.hook: Somewhere in the city, the real signal was already live.
involve:2.line: 'All his plans *involve* a trap you think is the exit.'

risk:2.en: Inside the flooded tunnel beneath Channel Seven's relay tower, I found a data chip wedged in a crack. Grey Crow's voice crackled in my earpiece: 'Don't touch it.' I touched it anyway. Sometimes you have to *risk* everything on a single move when the clock is already running out.
risk:2.cnHint: 在积水的隧道里，我发现了一枚数据芯片，决定冒____拿走它。
risk:2.hook: The chip blinked once, then the tunnel lights died.
risk:2.line: 'You *risk* everything the moment you pick that up,' Grey Crow warned.

success:2.en: Ali slid a crumpled paper across the wet bench — a printed signal map, channels marked in red ink. 'Someone decoded the broadcast before us,' she said quietly. The map was proof of their *success*, and it made my stomach drop. If they were this far ahead, we were already too late.
success:2.cnHint: 阿里找到一张信号地图，上面记录着别人破解广播的____。
success:2.hook: At the bottom of the map, my own name was circled.
success:2.line: 'Their *success* means we have no time left,' Ali said.

group:2.en: Hidden behind a vending machine on the forty-second floor, I watched a *group* of figures in grey coats exchange something small and flat. No words. No signals. Just a silent transfer. Grey Crow had warned me about them — people who traded in forbidden frequencies. Now I had faces.
group:2.cnHint: 我在四十二楼目击了一个神秘____悄悄交换禁播频道的东西。
group:2.hook: One of them slowly turned and looked straight at me.
group:2.line: 'That *group* moves only when a new channel goes dark,' Grey Crow said.

course:2.en: The investigation had taken a sharp turn. Zero had changed the broadcast *course* — the signal no longer looped through the harbor antenna. It cut inland, threading through old school buildings no one had used in decades. I followed the new path on my map, pulse fast, rain hammering the window.
course:2.cnHint: 零点改变了信号传输的____，我必须重新追踪路线。
course:2.hook: The trail ended at a classroom with one light still on.
course:2.line: 'He changed the *course* to throw us off the tower,' Ali said.

relationship:2.en: Pinned inside the relay box was a photograph — Grey Crow and Zero, standing together, younger, almost smiling. I had never imagined any *relationship* between them. The image was faded but the meaning was sharp: whatever they once shared had curdled into something cold and dangerous.
relationship:2.cnHint: 我在中继箱里发现了一张旧照片，揭示了灰鸦与零点之间隐藏的____。
relationship:2.hook: On the back, two words: 'Never again.'
relationship:2.line: 'Our *relationship* ended the night Channel Seven went silent,' Grey Crow said.

form:2.en: The message was not written in letters. It was a *form* pressed into the dust on the archive shelf — the outline of a key, deliberate and clean. Someone had been here, left this shape on purpose, and walked away knowing I would find it. I traced the edges with one finger.
form:2.cnHint: 档案室的灰尘上留着一个奇怪的____，那是一把钥匙的轮廓。
form:2.hook: The shelf behind it swung open without a sound.
form:2.line: 'This *form* is a message — someone wants you to follow,' Ali said.

interest:2.en: Zero's broadcast contained a list of names — citizens flagged for showing too much *interest* in Channel Seven. My name was not on it. That should have been a relief. Instead, it felt like a trap. If Zero already knew who I was, being left off that list meant something worse was planned for me.
interest:2.cnHint: 零点的广播列出了对第七频道表现出过多____的市民名单。
interest:2.hook: Ali went pale. Her name was third from the top.
interest:2.line: 'Your *interest* in Channel Seven has already been noticed,' Zero's voice said.

simply:2.en: Ali handed me the decoded file and I read it twice, then a third time. The truth was not complex. Channel Seven had been shut down because one man wanted the city *simply* silent — no coded talk, no signal art, no hidden voices. Power dressed up as quiet. That was all.
simply:2.cnHint: 解码文件揭示了第七频道被封锁的原因，答案____得令人心寒。
simply:2.hook: The man's name at the bottom was someone I trusted.
simply:2.line: 'He *simply* wanted no one left who could speak in code,' Ali said.

enable:2.en: Deep inside the old signal tower, I found a cracked data chip. Grey Crow had told me nothing about it. A faint label read: FREQ-07. Plugging it in would *enable* the dead Channel Seven broadcast — the one Zero had silenced three years ago. My hands wouldn't stop shaking.
enable:2.cnHint: 我在信号塔里发现一枚旧芯片，插入它将____第七频道重新广播。
enable:2.hook: The chip clicked in, and the walls started humming.
enable:2.line: 'This chip will *enable* the signal — if you're brave enough to use it.'

simple:2.en: The message was scratched onto a food-ration tin left on a wet bench outside the dockyard gate. No code, no cipher. Just twelve plain words. Ali leaned over my shoulder and read it twice. 'It looks too *simple*,' she said. Traps in Harbor City always wore clean faces.
simple:2.cnHint: 码头长椅上的锡罐留着一条看似____的留言，但阿里感到不安。
simple:2.hook: Under the tin, a second message was already dissolving in the rain.
simple:2.line: 'It looks too *simple* — someone wants us to stop thinking.'

several:2.en: The evidence room held *several* unmarked boxes stacked against the far wall. Each one was sealed with the same grey wax stamp — a crow in flight. I had counted them three times. Grey Crow said he had never been here. The wax told a different story.
several:2.cnHint: 证物室里有____个贴着灰色封印的箱子，与引路人的说法矛盾。
several:2.hook: The last box was still warm to the touch.
several:2.line: 'I found *several* sealed boxes — and your mark is on every one.'

struggle:2.en: The encrypted file was almost open. Every second, the decryption counter climbed one digit. Zero's counter-program clawed back two. I watched the numbers war across my screen, a quiet *struggle* measured in milliseconds. Ali cut the room's outside link. Now it was just us and the math.
struggle:2.cnHint: 我的破译程序与零点的反制程序之间展开了一场无声的____。
struggle:2.hook: At zero seconds remaining, both counters froze at once.
struggle:2.line: 'This *struggle* in the code — it means Zero is watching us right now.'

decision:2.en: Grey Crow placed two data cards on the table. One held the Channel Seven source files. The other held the names of everyone who had reported the signal. 'You can only take one,' he said quietly. I stared at both for a long moment. Every *decision* here cost someone something.
decision:2.cnHint: 引路人摆出两张数据卡，我必须做出一个沉重的____。
decision:2.hook: I reached out — and Grey Crow caught my wrist.
decision:2.line: 'Whatever your *decision* is, you cannot take it back after tonight.'

kid:2.en: Tucked inside the hollow relay post was a child's paper notebook, its cover drawn over with stick figures and signal towers. A *kid* had mapped every hidden antenna in the south district — by hand, in crayon, perfectly accurate. No adult in the department had that data. I felt cold.
kid:2.cnHint: 一本____的涂鸦本里藏着南区所有隐秘天线的精准地图。
kid:2.hook: On the last page, my name was written in small, careful letters.
kid:2.line: 'A *kid* drew this map — which means someone has been using children to watch us.'

ability:2.en: Zero's broadcast jammed every channel I tried. Ali rerouted through the old harbour grid. Still nothing. Then Grey Crow touched the console once, and Channel Seven opened like a door. His *ability* to move through blocked signals was something I had heard about but never believed until that moment.
ability:2.cnHint: 引路人展示出穿透封锁信号的____，令我第一次真正相信了传言。
ability:2.hook: Grey Crow pulled his hand back and said, 'Now Zero knows we are here.'
ability:2.line: 'Your *ability* to stay calm is the only thing keeping this channel alive.'

task:2.en: The file listed only three words under my name: LOCATE. RETRIEVE. TRANSMIT. Such a short *task* for something that had already swallowed two investigators before me. I read it again in the blue glow of the screen. Somewhere above the city, Channel Seven was still sending its signal into the dark.
task:2.cnHint: 档案里我的代号下只写了三个动词，概括了这项危险的____。
task:2.hook: Below the three words, someone had added a fourth: SURVIVE.
task:2.line: 'Your *task* is written down — but no one ever told you the real cost.'

popular:2.en: The coded broadcast on Channel Seven was *popular* across every district of Harbor City. Everyone tuned in, not for music, but for the hidden signals buried beneath the static. I found a folded paper in my coat pocket. Someone had slipped it there. It read: 'The most listened-to voice is the most dangerous one.'
popular:2.cnHint: 第七频道的广播在全城广受追捧，我口袋里悄然出现了一张神秘纸条，暗示____的声音最危险。
popular:2.hook: The paper dissolved in my fingers before I could show anyone.
popular:2.line: 'The most *popular* channel,' Grey Crow said, 'is the one they most want to silence.'

current:2.en: I picked up a small metal disc from the wet pavement near the old signal tower. Its surface hummed with a faint *current*, like a heartbeat trapped inside cold steel. Ali had warned me about objects like this — alive with hidden data, waiting for the right hands. These were the right hands.
current:2.cnHint: 我在信号塔旁捡到一枚金属圆盘，它带有微弱的____，仿佛储存着某种秘密。
current:2.hook: The disc grew warm, and a voice began to speak.
current:2.line: 'Feel that *current*,' Ali whispered. 'Someone is already sending a signal.'

difficult:2.en: The message was scratched onto the underside of a rusted vent cover deep in the Channel Seven relay station. The symbols were *difficult* to read — layered, shifting, built to confuse anyone who lacked the cipher key. I had the key. Zero knew that. Which meant Zero was already close.
difficult:2.cnHint: 我在中继站找到一条刻在通风口底部的信息，上面的符号极为____，需要密钥才能读懂。
difficult:2.hook: Behind me, a vent cover scraped open in the dark.
difficult:2.line: '*Difficult* is the point,' Zero said coldly. 'Easy messages get people caught.'

amount:2.en: Stacked inside the hollow base of a Channel Seven antenna was a sealed box. Inside: data chips, each holding a staggering *amount* of intercepted city-wide transmissions. Months of secrets. Years, maybe. Ali counted the chips in silence, her face pale under the neon glow filtering through the cracked ceiling above us.
amount:2.cnHint: 天线底座的暗格里藏着一个密封盒，里面存有惊人____的截获信号数据。
amount:2.hook: One chip was still warm — recorded less than an hour ago.
amount:2.line: 'The *amount* here,' Ali said quietly, 'is enough to bring down the whole network.'

point:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a thin stylus pulled from behind a loose wall panel in the relay room. The sharp *point* at its tip was not for writing — it was a scanner, designed to read the coded graffiti sprayed along the station walls. Each tag was a node. Each node was a name.
point:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我一支特制探针，它的____能够扫描墙上隐藏在涂鸦中的密码节点。
point:2.hook: The last name on the wall was mine.
point:2.line: 'Touch the *point* to the tag,' Grey Crow said. 'And do not pull back.'

role:2.en: Buried in the Channel Seven archive logs was a file with my name attached. I opened it with cold hands. It listed every move I had made since arriving in Harbor City. Someone had assigned me a *role* in this operation long before I ever volunteered — a part I had been playing without knowing the script.
role:2.cnHint: 我在频道七的存档记录中发现了自己的档案，原来我早已被安排了一个____，却毫不知情。
role:2.hook: The file's author was listed only as Zero.
role:2.line: 'Your *role*,' Zero's voice crackled through the static, 'was chosen before you were born.'

survey:2.en: The signal led me to a collapsed bridge on the edge of Sector Nine. Grey Crow handed me a scanner. 'You need to *survey* the whole underside,' he said. Rust and old paint flaked into the dark water below. Hidden among the beams, a small metal case blinked with a slow green light.
survey:2.cnHint: 在破旧的桥梁底部，我奉命____这片区域，却发现了一个神秘的金属盒子。
survey:2.hook: The case was still warm — someone had just left it.
survey:2.line: '*Survey* every beam before you touch anything,' Grey Crow warned.

care:2.en: Ali found the message folded inside a cracked street lamp near the old port. The paper was thin, almost falling apart. 'Handle it with *care*,' she said, passing it to me with steady hands. The words on it were not in any language I knew — yet somehow, I could read every line.
care:2.cnHint: 阿栗在路灯里发现了一张纸条，叮嘱我要____地对待它，而那张纸上的文字令人费解。
care:2.hook: The last word on the note was my own name.
care:2.line: 'Take *care* — this paper is older than the city itself,' Ali said.

state:2.en: Grey Crow's voice came through the earpiece, thin and broken. 'What is the *state* of the device?' he asked. I looked at the small box on the table: its screen was dark, its casing cracked, but one tiny red light still pulsed. Whatever it had carried, part of it was still alive.
state:2.cnHint: 灰鸦通过耳机询问设备的____，而那个小盒子虽然破损，却仍有信号在跳动。
state:2.hook: The red light blinked once — then spelled a name.
state:2.line: 'Tell me the exact *state* of the device — nothing left out,' Grey Crow said.

impact:2.en: The encrypted file arrived at midnight, buried inside a routine weather broadcast. Ali and I opened it together in the back room of a closed noodle shop. The data inside showed the *impact* of a deleted signal on the city's entire communication grid — whole districts had gone silent for six minutes, seven years ago.
impact:2.cnHint: 一份加密文件揭示了某次信号删除事件对全市通讯网络的____，阿栗和我都震惊了。
impact:2.hook: Six silent minutes — and twelve people had vanished that night.
impact:2.line: 'The *impact* was larger than anyone reported,' Ali said quietly.

reason:2.en: I found the old notebook under a loose floor tile in the archive room. Most pages were blank, but one line repeated across three pages: 'There is a *reason* the seventh channel was sealed.' No name, no date. Grey Crow had told me the channel was closed due to noise. He had clearly lied.
reason:2.cnHint: 档案室的笔记本里反复出现同一句话，暗示第七频道被封锁有其____，而灰鸦对我隐瞒了真相。
reason:2.hook: On the final page, someone had drawn my face.
reason:2.line: 'There is a *reason* no one goes to that channel,' Grey Crow said flatly.

close:2.en: The signal trace ended at a small door behind the market's power station. Ali checked her scanner. 'We are *close*,' she said, her voice low. The door had no handle, only a panel of worn keys. Rain hit the metal roof above us in hard, fast drops. Inside, something was broadcasting.
close:2.cnHint: 信号追踪把我们带到了一扇隐蔽的小门前，阿栗说我们已经很____目标了，门内仍有信号在发出。
close:2.hook: The broadcast inside was using my personal access code.
close:2.line: 'We are *close* — do not make a sound,' Ali whispered.

individual:2.en: The city registry listed nine people who had accessed the seventh channel before it was sealed. Grey Crow pulled up their files on a cracked wall screen. 'Each *individual* on this list disappeared within a month,' he said. Eight files had a red mark. The ninth file — the most recent — had no mark yet.
individual:2.cnHint: 名单上的每一个____在接触第七频道后都神秘失踪了，而第九份档案至今没有标记。
individual:2.hook: The ninth file showed a photo — it was Ali.
individual:2.line: 'Every *individual* on this list made the same mistake,' Grey Crow said.

area:2.en: The signal was strongest near the old water tower in the north *area* of the port district. I climbed the iron stairs alone, scanner in hand. The reading spiked at the top — something was transmitting from inside the tower's sealed upper room. The lock on the door was brand new.
area:2.cnHint: 港区北部____的信号最强，我独自爬上水塔，发现封闭房间里有东西正在发射信号，而门锁是新的。
area:2.hook: A new lock on a sealed room meant someone had just been here.
area:2.line: 'Stay in the *area* — the signal will peak again in three minutes,' Ali said.

put:2.en: The sealed box sat on the wet floor of the old signal station. Ali pointed at the lock. I *put* my ear against the metal side and heard it — a low hum, coded pulses, a message meant for no one alive. Someone had left this here on purpose. The question was when.
put:2.cnHint: 我将耳朵贴近金属箱，____到冷金属上，听见了里面隐藏的编码脉冲。
put:2.hook: The hum stopped the moment I touched the lock.
put:2.line: '*Put* your ear here — tell me what you hear.'

difference:2.en: Two copies of the same city map were pinned to the wall of Grey Crow's safe room. I stared for a long minute. Then I saw it — one small street, erased from the newer print. That single *difference* meant one route existed in the real city that the official grid refused to show. Someone had scrubbed it clean.
difference:2.cnHint: 两张地图上有一处____，那条被抹去的街道隐藏着秘密通道。
difference:2.hook: Grey Crow whispered: that street leads straight to Zero.
difference:2.line: 'The *difference* between these two maps is the only truth left.'

lack:2.en: Ali spread the decoded files across the table. Good data on Zero's broadcast towers, solid timing logs, clean signal traces. But one thing was missing. The *lack* of any sender ID made the whole case shaky. Without a name attached to the source, we had noise, not proof. Zero had been careful.
lack:2.cnHint: 这些解码文件中____发送者身份信息，让整个案件站不稳脚。
lack:2.hook: Ali tapped one blank field and said nothing.
lack:2.line: 'This *lack* of ID is not an accident — it is a message.'

case:2.en: Grey Crow slid a thin metal folder across the table. 'This *case* started three years before you joined,' she said. Inside: six burned signal towers, forty-one intercepted words, one name that kept appearing and disappearing like smoke. I was not the first investigator on this. I might not be the last.
case:2.cnHint: 灰鸦递来的案件____卷宗显示，这个调查早在我加入前就开始了。
case:2.hook: The last investigator's name had been crossed out in red.
case:2.line: 'This *case* is older than you think — and far from closed.'

sure:2.en: The graffiti on the tunnel wall read: CHANNEL SEVEN KNOWS. I photographed it fast and sent it to Ali. I was not *sure* whether it was a warning or an invitation — in Harbor City the two things often wore the same face. I pressed deeper into the tunnel anyway. The signal in my head was getting louder.
sure:2.cnHint: 我不____这段涂鸦是警告还是邀请，但隧道深处的信号越来越强。
sure:2.hook: At the tunnel's end, a light blinked on — once, twice, then nothing.
sure:2.line: 'Are you *sure* you want to follow that signal alone?'

enough:2.en: Ali had cracked four layers of Zero's encryption by midnight. She leaned back and pressed her eyes shut. 'That is *enough* for tonight,' she said, but her screen still glowed, and the fifth layer was already loading. I watched her hands move back to the keys without her seeming to notice. Some things pull you in.
enough:2.cnHint: 阿栗说今晚的解密工作已经____了，但她的双手却不由自主地继续敲击键盘。
enough:2.hook: The fifth layer opened — and inside was our names.
enough:2.line: '*Enough* rest — the fifth layer just unlocked itself.'

attention:2.en: Zero broadcast a false weather report at 03:00, city-wide. Everyone heard it. But it was designed to draw *attention* away from a second, smaller signal sent two seconds later on a dead channel. I caught that second signal. Grey Crow had taught me to listen for the quiet thing hiding behind the loud one.
attention:2.cnHint: 虚假广播吸引了所有人的____，而零号在两秒后发出的微弱信号才是真正的信息。
attention:2.hook: The small signal carried three words: I see you.
attention:2.line: 'Pay *attention* to what Zero does not want you to hear.'

certain:2.en: I replayed the recording four times before I let myself believe it. Grey Crow's voice, no question. But *certain* words were reversed, certain pauses were wrong. It was not a real broadcast — it was a copy, rebuilt from pieces. Someone had learned how she spoke and made a weapon out of it. Ali went pale.
certain:2.cnHint: 录音中____些词语的顺序和停顿都不对，这不是灰鸦真正的声音。
certain:2.hook: Ali said: if they can fake her voice, they can fake anyone's.
certain:2.line: 'I am *certain* — that voice was built, not recorded.'
